Hi Hannah — great to chat today. Thanks for walking us through Acme's latency and throughput goals for the in-store recommendation API. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key points and next steps so we can align on SLO targets and draft SLA language.

Recap (from your team):
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent inference requests per region during Black Friday testing; steady-state concurrency ~25–40.
- Desired latency targets: P95 <= 200ms for single-request non-streaming inference; P99 targets are nice-to-have but tolerant to some higher variance during spikes.
- Streaming use case: voice-to-text + progressive scoring for checkout flow; streaming chunk latency target is < 150ms per chunk with total session latency expectations lower priority.
- Throughput: baseline throughput of ~200 reqs/sec across three regions, with burst capacity to 800 reqs/sec for short windows.
- Reporting / remedies: your procurement wants explicit measurement methodology, exclusions (maintenance, force majeure), reporting cadence, and proposed service-credit remedies tied to monthly availability/latency SLO misses.

Our action items
1) Rishi to provide a technical note on how Redwood measures latency (what's included/excluded), streaming metrics, and recommendations for P95/P99 targets.
2) Marissa/Dylan to draft SLA language and propose reporting cadence and remedies; share a first draft for your legal/procurement to review.
3) Align on a mutual action plan and sign-off timeline — you mentioned wanting a redline by early next week if possible.

Attachments: I'm uploading a draft action plan and initial SLA template for review (attached).

Next steps: Rishi, can you comment on measurement approach and preliminary SLO suggestions? Hannah/Alex, does this capture the priorities correctly and is the redline-by-next-week timeline workable?

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures the conversation. A few clarifying questions from procurement/ops so our legal team can prepare a redline: 

1) Measurement: when you say P95 <= 200ms, is that measured at the Redwood edge (time request accepted by Redwood to final token emitted) or end-to-end including client network time? We need precise language to avoid ambiguity.
2) Streaming: for the voice scoring flow we stream partial transcripts and incremental scores. Do you measure per-chunk latency, or overall session latency? If per-chunk, how do you define a chunk boundary?
3) Exclusions: we expect scheduled maintenance windows to be excluded, but what about short-lived autoscaling delays during warmups? Also need to confirm the blackout windows during major retail events (we'll provide dates).
4) Remedies: procurement prefers a tiered service credit tied to monthly P95 breaches rather than a flat dollar amount. Can you propose a sample schedule?

If you can draft a short technical note answering the three measurement/streaming/exclusion points, and a sample remedies table, that will speed legal review. We can target a redline by next Thursday (28 Oct) — is that ok?

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Hannah — following up with the technical details Marissa requested. Below is a concise note you can include in the SLA appendix; happy to expand if legal needs more precise definitions.

Latency measurement (recommended language):
- Definition: Latency is measured at the Redwood ingress gateway timestamp when request is first accepted by the Redwood runtime to the timestamp when the final inference token is emitted (server-side processing time). This measurement excludes client-side network transit, CDN routing outside Redwood, and any client pre-processing time.
- Aggregation windows: Percentiles (P50/P95/P99) are computed over 1-minute buckets and reported as the percentile over the calendar month. P95 is the 95th percentile of all 1-minute bucket medians across the month (or alternatively computed over raw per-request measurements — we can pick consistent method).

Streaming behavior and chunking: 
- Chunk definition: For streaming APIs we define a chunk as any incremental server-emitted packet containing a partial transcript or token batch. Per-chunk latency is measured from ingress acceptance to the chunk emission. For session-level SLAs, we recommend focusing on per-chunk P95 (e.g., P95 per-chunk <= 150ms) and include a soft session-level target (e.g., median session completion time).

Concurrency/throughput notes:
- Concurrency is counted as concurrent active inference sessions/rpc connections observed at the Redwood runtime. Burst capacities are supported via autoscaling, but warm-up windows (configurable) may see degraded latency as new nodes attach to the runtime; we recommend explicitly listing a short warm-up exclusion (e.g., first 5 minutes of autoscale events) in the SLA.

Exclusions and scheduled maintenance:
- Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance windows (with >=72 hours notice) and force majeure events are excluded. Short autoscaling warm-up windows (first X minutes of a scale event) can be excluded if both parties agree on warm-up durations; Redwood proposes a default 5-minute warm-up exclusion for scale-up events.

Reporting cadence and remedies:
- Reporting: Redwood will provide weekly latency/availability reports and a consolidated monthly SLA report with raw percentile data and an explanation for any breaches.
- Remedies: Sample schedule (monthly):
  - If monthly P95 <= target: 0% credit
  - If monthly P95 > target but <= target + 20%: 5% service credit
  - If monthly P95 > target + 20%: 15% service credit
  - Repeat breaches or extended outages escalate to formal remediation planning (on-site/troubleshoot cadence).

Draft SLA attachments: Marissa attached an initial SLA template (redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf). I'm also attaching a short action plan spreadsheet mapping responsibilities and dates. Marissa — we can tighten the percentile computation language depending on legal preference (raw per-request vs per-minute buckets).

Happy to jump on a short technical sync if you want to walk through the measurement math.

Thanks — Rishi
